short: Anne Boleyn was the second wife of Henry VIII, whose marriage led to the English Reformation, and who was executed for treason.
full:
Returning to England after serving in the French court, Anne Boleyn captivated Henry VIII. Her refusal to become his mistress, insisting instead on marriage, drove Henry's momentous effort to annul his first marriage. When the Pope refused, Henry broke from Rome and established the Church of England, marrying Anne in 1533 and crowning her queen. She soon gave birth to a daughter, the future Elizabeth I, but her failure to provide a male heir quickly eroded her position.

Anne was a patron of reformist scholars and played a crucial role in advancing early Protestant ideas in England. However, by 1536, she had alienated powerful courtiers, notably Thomas Cromwell. Accused of treason, adultery, and incest in a highly dubious trial, she was beheaded at the Tower of London, marking the first time an English queen had been publicly executed.
